title: 5 Ways to Build User-Friendly Web3 Applications
summary: Learn 5 strategies to build web3 applications that attract and delight users.
author: Nathaniel Thoreson
body:
For years, the builders in the Web3 industry have chased a goal that still alludes them: Mass Adoption.

Billions of dollars and man-hours have been poured into products that founders hope will cause millions of users to race to join web3. But it's yet to happen. User growth remains sluggish, especially during the bear market.

But, it's not all bad news. Web3's slow user adoption isn't a new phenomenon in the tech industry. With a history in mind, web3's adoption curve is predictable. With time and some elbow grease, the ship can be turned in the right direction. 

In the late 1990s, the proverbial ship was turning as the internet went through a transformational moment leading to a massive influx of first-time users. Internet companies began the transition away from building products that only fellow computer nerds would care about. They shifted to building products for the everyday user. 

In the mid-2000s, the transition reached its peak when Facebook attracted billions of first-time users. Its smooth UI and clear value proposition were incredibly appealing to people around the world. For many of them, Facebook was their first introduction to the broader landscape of the internet. 

Web3 has yet to create the next Mark Zuckerberg. No single builder or product has attracted billions of users which will make Web3 a worldwide phenomenon.

At the moment, web3 founders are focused on creating novel technologies that have no appeal to a broader audience besides their fellow crypto degens with no focus on the user experience, design, or value prop for the users. 

As a result, web3 remains out of reach for billions. 

It's time to usher in the next stage of web3, one where billions of users flock. I have faith that you, dear reader, could lead the charge.

Today, we'll explain five ways you can build a web3 product that delights users and keeps them coming back, even if they've never used a web3 product before. By employing these strategies, you can replicate Facebook's climb to the top and become a force of change for the whole industry.

Be sure to read to the end. Number Five will speed up your web3 development time by 10x, even if you can't code.

‍

1 - Delight your users with UI/UX

We all know what it's like to use a badly designed product. After a few minutes of trying to understand it, we leave never to return. For Web3 applications, creating a beautiful UI (user interface) and a quality UX (user experience) are doubly important. Getting into crypto and Web3 is hard enough for everyday people. Don't let bad UI/UX make it even harder. 

Poor UI/UX can make your product seem spammy and low quality. Investing the time to study and implement best UI/UX practices is key to building user trust and brand loyalty.

So, what makes a great UI/UX? It's all about making your application easy to use and navigate. Remember, Web3 technology can be confusing for people everyday people. So, you want to make it as user-friendly as possible. 

Do this by conducting user testing, getting feedback, and improving your product based on that feedback. You'll quickly learn how powerful a quality interface will delight your users. Soon you'll be on the right track to building a successful web3 business with customers yearning for more.


2- Sell the benefits, not the tech:

Let's be honest. Most people don't care about the blockchain tech powering your app. They want to know how your product can solve their problems and make their lives easier. So, instead of focusing on the technical details, focus on the benefits of your product.

What does your Web3 application do? How does it make people's lives easier or more efficient? These are the questions you need to answer when marketing your product. 

Avoid using technical jargon that might confuse non-technical users. 

Did Zuckerberg try to sell Facebook by explaining how the internet works? Of course not, he crafted a beautiful product that had a clear value proposition.

Most importantly, deliver on your messaging. Tell people why your web3 product will make their lives better and then actually do it.

Remember, show, don't tell.
